knowledge:
- key_parameters: CancerSite=The TCGA cancer code (e.g., "LIHC") used to download data ;; TargetDirectory=The local directory path where downloaded TCGA data is saved ;; NrModules=The number of co-expressed gene modules to construct (recommends 100 for a first run) ;; VarPercentage=The percentage of most varying genes to use for clustering (recommends top 25%) ;; MA_Data_TestSet=Centered and scaled gene expression matrix for independent test set evaluation ;; RegulatorData_TestSet=Regulator data matrix for independent test set evaluation ;; hyper_geo_reference=Path to a GMT file containing gene sets for hypergeometric enrichment testing
- alternatives: MethylMix is mentioned as the package used to process raw DNA methylation data to produce the methylation states used by AMARETTO
- when_to_use: Use when integrating multi-omics cancer data (gene expression, DNA copy number, and DNA methylation) to identify driver genes and co-expressed gene modules, ideally with a cohort of at least 100 samples where all three modalities are present
- pitfalls: Independent test sets must be centered and scaled to unit variance before running evaluation ;; Missing regulators in the test dataset due to platform limitations will adversely affect the Rsquare performance ;; Running AMARETTO on very large cohorts (e.g., BRCA) is computationally intensive and can take up to an hour to converge

workflows.name: amaretto_multi_omics_pipeline
workflows.intent: Download TCGA multi-omics data, preprocess it, run the AMARETTO algorithm to identify driver-connected co-expressed gene modules, evaluate the model, and generate visualizations/reports.
input: CancerSite (string identifier for TCGA cancer type)
BatchData (Rda file containing batch correction data)
gmt_file (GMT file containing gene sets for enrichment analysis)
workflows.stages: 1. Download TCGA data using AMARETTO_Download ;; 2. Preprocess the downloaded data using AMARETTO_Preprocess ;; 3. Initialize the AMARETTO algorithm using AMARETTO_Initialize ;; 4. Run the AMARETTO algorithm using AMARETTO_Run ;; 5. Evaluate the model on a test set using AMARETTO_EvaluateTestSet ;; 6. Visualize specific modules using AMARETTO_VisualizeModule ;; 7. Generate an HTML report with gene set enrichment using AMARETTO_HTMLreport
workflows.code:
library(AMARETTO)
TargetDirectory <- tempfile()# data download directory
CancerSite <- "LIHC"
DataSetDirectories <- AMARETTO_Download(CancerSite = CancerSite,
                                        TargetDirectory = TargetDirectory)
load("../inst/extdata/MethylStates.rda")
ProcessedData <- AMARETTO_Preprocess(DataSetDirectories = DataSetDirectories,
                                    BatchData = BatchData)
library(AMARETTO)
data(ProcessedDataLIHC)
AMARETTOinit <- AMARETTO_Initialize(ProcessedData = ProcessedDataLIHC,
                                    NrModules = 2, VarPercentage = 50)
AMARETTOresults <- AMARETTO_Run(AMARETTOinit = AMARETTOinit)
AMARETTOtestReport <- AMARETTO_EvaluateTestSet(
                      AMARETTOresults = AMARETTOresults,
                      MA_Data_TestSet = AMARETTOinit$MA_matrix_Var,
                      RegulatorData_TestSet = AMARETTOinit$RegulatorData
                      )
ModuleNr <- 1 #define the module number to visualize

AMARETTO_VisualizeModule(AMARETTOinit = AMARETTOinit, 
                         AMARETTOresults = AMARETTOresults,
                         ProcessedData = ProcessedDataLIHC, 
                         ModuleNr = ModuleNr)
gmt_file<-system.file("templates/H.C2CP.genesets.gmt",package="AMARETTO")
AMARETTO_HTMLreport(AMARETTOinit = AMARETTOinit,,
                    AMARETTOresults = AMARETTOresults,
                    ProcessedData = ProcessedDataLIHC,
                    hyper_geo_test_bool = TRUE,
                    hyper_geo_reference = gmt_file,
                    MSIGDB=TRUE)
